jobs.title: Sr. Worldwide Program Manager, Data & AI GTM
jobs.description:
Description

This isn't your typical program management role. You'll be the person who ensures the infrastructure behind AWS's Data & AI sales plays actually works, and works well. That means holding a high bar on sales play templates, bill of materials quality, reporting, and content management so that everything the AWS sales field touches is accurate, up-to-date, and ready to drive impact. You'll own and continuously improve the knowledge base of sales plays, reusable content, and industry use cases that enables our sellers, and the agentic experiences that assist them, to help customers faster and more effectively. Think of this role as running the center of excellence for Data & AI sales plays: setting the standard, maintaining the system, and making sure what we put in front of AWS field teams and assistance agents is always sharp and current.

You'll drive global GTM initiatives from the ground up, identifying where the biggest opportunities are, packaging them into repeatable motions, and making sure they land with impact across regions and industries. If a sales team in financial services needs a sharper AI use case to unlock a deal, or if healthcare needs a data play that resonates with CIOs, that's your infrastructure and content showing up in the field.

What makes this role different is the scope and the leverage. You're not supporting one team or one product. You're shaping how AWS's entire Data & AI story gets organized, maintained, and delivered across the globe. You'll work across product, business development, solutions architecture, marketing, sales, and partner teams to make that happen, and you'll see your impact in real numbers: pipeline created, deals accelerated, revenue driven.

If you like building systems that scale, thrive in ambiguity, and want to work at the intersection of program rigor and GTM execution in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech, this is the job.

Key job responsibilities

Serve as the center of excellence for Data & AI sales plays, setting and enforcing standards for sales play templates, completion, bills of materials, use case documentation, content management, and quality across the portfolio
Own and continuously improve the knowledge base of sales plays, reusable content, and industry use cases that enables our sales field and assistance agents to help customers more effectively
Influence cross-functional teams to design, build, and scale repeatable sales plays while driving a high bar for bills of materials that directly address friction points in the customer sales cycle, delivered through both traditional methods and agentic experiences
Manage sales play and use case reporting, tracking performance metrics like pipeline generated, sales acceleration, and win/revenue realization rates, and continuously iterating based on what the data and anecdotes tell you
Help develop industry-focused use cases (e.g., financial services, healthcare, manufacturing) that show customers exactly how AWS Data & AI solves their specific challenges
Partner cross-functionally with product, solutions architecture, marketing, sales, and partner teams to ensure GTM initiatives are aligned, resourced, and landing with impact across regions
Ensure the infrastructure of sales acceleration content is accurate, current, and structured to power both human sellers and agentic experiences at scale
Drive executive-level alignment on GTM priorities, making the case for where to invest and ensuring stakeholders across the business are rowing in the same direction

A day in the life

Your morning might start with a call reviewing pipeline data to see which sales plays are gaining traction and which need retooling. By mid-morning, you're in a working session with product and marketing teams, pressure-testing a new set of industry use case for financial services before it goes live to the field. After lunch, you're collaborating with a specialist sales leader in Australia who's seeing friction in a deal cycle and needs a sharper bill of materials — and you're figuring out how to deliver it both through traditional enablement channels and agentic experiences. Late afternoon, you're pulling together an executive memo that makes the case for doubling down on a GTM motion that's outperforming expectations. No two days look the same, but the throughline is always the same: connecting strategy to execution and making sure what you build actually moves numbers.

About The Team

We're a worldwide team that sits at the crossroads of AWS's Data & AI portfolio, working across categories rather than within a single product lane. Our job is to take everything AWS offers in the Data & AI space and package it into GTM sales motions that are clear, compelling, and easy for the AWS field to execute. That means driving campaigns, sales plays, field activations, and sales incentives, and doing it in close partnership with marketing, product, business development, and solutions architecture teams. We connect a lot of dots so that when a sales play lands in the hands of field teams anywhere in the world, it's sharp, complete, and ready to drive pipeline. If you like working horizontally across big organizations and turning complexity into simplicity, you'll feel right at home here.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
Knowledge of general AI tools

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Experience driving global sales enablement programs that equip field teams with the tools, messaging, and content they need to execute effectively
Experience leading or contributing to organizational transformation efforts where you've helped teams adopt new ways of working, shift mindsets, or stand up entirely new operating models

jobs.title: Data Analyst - Non-Remote
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Healthcare Operations Data Analyst should have an understanding of process improvement methodologies and the utilization of data analysis within those methodologies. A good understanding of the utilization of statistical analysis to identify healthcare process improve opportunities and to determine successful workflow modifications is important. The Healthcare Operations Data Analyst should be capable of making specific recommendations for process improvements based upon rigorous analysis.

Job Summary:
The Data Analyst uses advanced analysis skills to enable the delivery of improved operational, clinical or business results. Is responsible for assisting members of the Operation Excellence department, as well as administrative and clinical operational leaders across LLUMC with achieving identified performance improvement initiatives. Is responsible for gathering, manipulating, analyzing and managing data to assist in the identification of operational opportunities that will have a positive impact on patient flow and/or the bottom line through reduction in cost or increase in revenue. Has excellent communication, analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills. Performs other duties as needed.

Education and Experience:
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Business, Mathematics, Finance or related field required. Minimum two years of data analysis experience.

Knowledge and Skills:
Advanced skills in using one or more data analysis software packages (e.g. MS Excel, SAS, Minitab, etc.). Specific expertise in Tableau, SQL and EPIC’s Cogito environment. Ability to provide functional direction and insights based on the interpretation of data. Able to work efficiently with Visualization and ETL developers in preparing and presenting complex analyses using data from EPIC. Able to read; write legibly; speak in English with professional quality. Operate/troubleshoot basic office equipment required for the position. Able to relate and communicate positively, effectively, and professionally with others; work calmly and respond courteously when under pressure; collaborate and accept direction. Able to communicate effectively in English in person, in writing, and on the telephone; think critically; manage multiple assignments effectively; organize and prioritize workload; work well under pressure; problem solve; recall information with accuracy; pay close attention to detail; work independently with minimal supervision. Able to distinguish colors as necessary; hear sufficiently for general conversation in person and on the telephone and identify and distinguish various sounds associated with the workplace; see adequately to read computer screens, and written documents necessary to the position.

Licensures and Certifications:
None.

About Us

Our mission is to continue the teaching and healing ministry of Jesus Christ. Our core values are compassion, excellence, humility, integrity, justice, teamwork and wholeness.

About The Team

Loma Linda University Health is a Seventh-day Adventist, faith and values based Christian institution. Candidates must understand and embrace the mission, purpose, and identity of Loma Linda and its affiliated entities.

We provide equal opportunities in all aspects of the employment process to every individual, regardless of gender, race, color, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, marital or veteran status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. In addition, we will provide reasonable accommodations for otherwise qualified individuals requesting an accommodation due to a disability. If you need accommodation assistance with accessing our job listings or completing an application, or during any other phase of employment with us, please contact Human Resources Management at (909) 651-4001.

No question on this application is asked for the purpose of unlawfully limiting or excluding any applicant’s consideration for employment because of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, disability, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. If you need a reasonable accommodation in the hiring process, please notify Human Resource Management.

jobs.description:
We are Lenovo. We do what we say. We own what we do. We WOW our customers.

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Focused on a bold vision to deliver Smarter Technology for All, Lenovo has built on its success as the world’s largest PC company with a full-stack portfolio of AI-enabled, AI-ready, and AI-optimized devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets), infrastructure (server, storage, edge, high performance computing and software defined infrastructure), software, solutions, and services. Lenovo’s continued investment in world-changing innovation is building a more equitable, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY).

This transformation together with Lenovo’s world-changing innovation is building a more inclusive, trustworthy, and smarter future for everyone, everywhere. To find out more visit www.lenovo.com, and read about the latest news via our StoryHub.

This position will be part of the headquarters of the International Sales Organization. The Project Manager will facilitate and own the delivery of key strategic, complex and diverse projects to support the achievement of the channel ecosystem transformation and harmonization strategic objectives. 

Working with multiple teams across worldwide business units, sales and channel teams, this individual will be responsible for the end-to-end management of projects, defining and owning the BMS, organizing and motivating the project team and the identification and delivery of solutions with strong mindset of outcome-based execution.

This position calls for a channel management experienced professional who can challenge the status quo, lead changes, drive commitments to keep timelines and is able to communicate to all levels in the business. The ability to independently manage complex interactions and situations is essential. This position will report to the Project Management Director based in China.

Key Responsibilities

Build and lead transformational projects for the International Sales and Channel Organization
Own and drive all aspects of project management activity, managing key strategic projects across multiple teams within the international sales teams, Lenovo geographies and business units
Work within the framework of standard Project Management methodology processes, tools, and documentation throughout the project lifecycle
Lead the project team, drive the key initiatives and actions to resolve roadblocks and deliver the committed project results
Drive substantial business improvement and enhance partner and customer experience through solid project planning, complex problem solving and innovative thinking
Provide clear and transparent communication to key stakeholders at all stages of the project
Manage multiple, medium to large projects with varying complexity

Required Qualifications Experience

Five plus years of experience in project management in large, multi-national, preferably tech organizations
Three plus years of experience in channel management or channel operations related work
Strong ability to manage complex projects with multiple stakeholders
Demonstrable transformation or strategic change skills with high solution orientation
Excellent cross group collaboration skills and proven ability to lead a virtual team located in multiple countries, experience in an international working environment is preferred
Strong verbal and written communications skills and ability to articulate complex concepts to cross-functional audiences including the senior leadership team
Self-starter mentality with a high degree of follow through - can own and take tasks through to completion
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
Professional fluency in English

What We Can Offer You

Holiday purchase 
Private medical 
Income protection
Attractive pension scheme 
Positive work life balance
Learning and development
Life insurance
Lenovo and Motorola products discounts 
Lifestyle discounts 
Cycle to work 
MyGymDiscounts
Mortgage advice and support 
Referral bonus
Free onsite parking

What You Will Be Doing

Own intake, triage, routing and request-quality standards for accelerator-capacity requests across multiple engineering and research teams.
Run quarterly and annual demand forecasts, change control, review preparation, and follow-through; identify late, incomplete, or conflicting inputs early.
Prepare capacity-planning and allocation reviews using demand, available supply, prior commitments, readiness, workload timing, and business priorities.
Track capacity through its operational lifecycle—from request and forecast through delivery, readiness, assignment, and productive use.
Coordinate infrastructure dependencies such as access, storage, data movement, networking, readiness checks, migration timing, and provider or provisioning tickets.
Maintain dashboards and source-data quality, including freshness checks, ownership for missing inputs, reconciliation, and retirement of repeated manual reporting.
Own operating cadences, agendas, action logs, dependency tracking, decision records, risk registers, blocking issue paths, and closure difficulty.
Prepare concise leadership reporting that distinguishes facts, risks, decisions needed, options, recommended paths, accountable owners, and due dates.

What We Need To See

BS/MS/PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering or similar (or equivalent experience).
7+ years of technical program management or closely related experience in AI/ML platforms, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, compute capacity, or another technically demanding engineering environment.

Strong program mechanics: intake compose, forecasting, review preparation, dependency management, decision and risk records, action closure, documentation, and status communication.
Enough technical proficiency to understand infrastructure constraints, ask detailed questions, inspect requirements and metrics, and work credibly with engineers and researchers.
Data proficiency sufficient to evaluate source quality, interpret dashboards, reconcile conflicting views, define useful operational measures, and identify missing ownership.

Ability to influence without authority across research, platform engineering, infrastructure, data, finance, operations, and leadership collaborators!

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with GPU or other accelerator-capacity planning, utilization programs, cluster operations, workload bring-up, or large-scale AI training and inference environments.
Experience with demand and supply roadmaps, normalization across accelerator types, allocation reviews, quota or priority management, and capacity migrations.

Experience driving API-enabled workflow automation or decision-support tools with explicit human approval gates, audit evidence, and safe operating controls.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline:
18 September 2026

Department:
OPS-Information Technology

Employment Type:
Permanent - Full Time

Location:
Remote

Reporting To:
SVP, Chief Technology Officer

Compensation:
$105,000 - $135,000 / year

Description

The Technical Project Manager (TPM) serves as the primary interface between JED's Salesforce delivery team and every department across the organization. This role owns intake, requirements definition, and stakeholder management for all CRM-related projects and requests, translating organizational needs into clearly scoped, ready-to-work deliverables for the Salesforce team. Working in close partnership with the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead, the TPM ensures that departments across JED, particularly ACE (Development/Fundraising), receive consistent, well-managed project support while protecting the Salesforce delivery team's capacity to execute planned work. This role requires someone who can speak fluently to fundraising and development stakeholders, hold firm boundaries around scope and readiness, and bring increased structure to a high-volume, cross-functional intake process.

Key Responsibilities

Intake, Requirements & Scoping

Serve as the first point of contact for any incoming request or project from any department (ACE, Marketing & Communications, School Programs, Product)
Schedule, coordinate, and facilitate scoping and requirements-gathering meetings with stakeholders
Gather requirements and translate them into clear acceptance criteria, user stories, and tasks
Define what “done” and “ready to work” mean for each incoming request before it reaches the delivery team

Stakeholder Management & Communication

Hold boundaries with stakeholders, communicating when a request isn’t ready or timelines need to shift
Host weekly office hours, either per department or grouped by related departments, to help teams plan upcoming work and proactively surface dependencies, deadlines, and resource conflicts
Manage expectations proactively, ensuring stakeholders understand project status, scope, and delivery timing
Build credibility and fluency with fundraising and development teams (ACE) to translate their needs accurately into technical requirements

Project & Delivery Coordination

Participate in Salesforce Delivery Team daily standups, backlog refinement, and sprint planning
Structure and maintain the Asana delivery board so intake, prioritization, and status are always visible and current
Manage day-to-day project tracking, sequencing, and status once work is defined and scoped
Coordinate handoffs between requirements definition and technical execution, looping in the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead on strategy, architecture or roadmap alignment as needed
Track and report on growth-related metrics tied to CRM-driven initiatives (e.g., donor growth, campaign performance, fundraising pipeline movement) to help departments and leadership understand the impact of delivered work

Functional Ownership

This role owns the intake, requirements-definition, and stakeholder-management function for JED's CRM/Salesforce environment. The TPM is accountable for the health and clarity of the project pipeline, including how requests enter the system, how they're scoped, and how stakeholders are communicated with throughout delivery. This role does not own technical configuration, Salesforce administration, or platform architecture; those remain with the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead and the Salesforce Administration team.

Decision Rights & Collaboration

Decides independently: whether an incoming request is sufficiently scoped and ready to enter the delivery pipeline; sequencing and prioritization of intake and requirements-gathering work; day-to-day stakeholder communication and expectation-setting; structure and maintenance of the delivery board.

Requires input or approval: final architecture or platform-strategy decisions (owned by the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead); prioritization calls that affect the broader team's workload (made in partnership with the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead); scope changes that expand a project beyond CRM/Salesforce.

Collaborates closely with: the CRM Strategy & Operations Lead, to ensure scoped projects align with overall CRM roadmap and architecture; the Salesforce Administration team, to hand off clearly defined, ready-to-work tasks; department stakeholders (especially ACE), as the primary point of contact for requests, requirements, and status updates.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

Required

Extremely well-versed in Salesforce, with strong working knowledge of the platform's capabilities, limitations, and common configurations (prior hands-on Salesforce experience strongly preferred, even if not in an administrator capacity)
Demonstrated experience in fundraising, development, or philanthropy, with the ability to speak credibly to development staff about donor management, campaigns, and fundraising workflows
3-5 years of project management or business analyst experience within a Salesforce, CRM, or nonprofit fundraising/development environment (required)
Proven experience managing technology or CRM projects from intake through delivery, including gathering requirements, defining acceptance criteria, and managing stakeholder expectations
Experience tracking and reporting on growth metrics (e.g., donor growth, fundraising performance, or similar KPIs tied to CRM data)
Excellent communication skills, with demonstrated ability to hold boundaries and manage competing stakeholder demands without escalating every conflict
Strong organizational skills and comfort working in project management tools (Asana or similar)
Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a technical delivery team

Preferred

Project management certification (e.g., PMP, CAPM)
Salesforce certification (e.g., Administrator, Business Analyst)
Direct experience working in a nonprofit development or fundraising department
Familiarity with Google Workspace, Slack, and Gearset

Success Metrics

Success will be measured across three areas.

Intake & Delivery Health

Requests move from intake to "ready to work" status within a consistent, defined timeframe, and the delivery board reflects accurate, current status at all times.

Stakeholder Trust & Expectation Management

Departments report clear understanding of project status and timelines, measured through stakeholder feedback and a reduction in escalations or ad hoc requests routed outside the intake process.

Growth Impact

CRM-driven initiatives show measurable contributions to organizational growth metrics (e.g., donor growth, campaign performance) that this role helped track and surface to stakeholders and leadership.

Salary Range (by Location):

New York (Geo A): $105,000 - 135,000
San Francisco (Geo SF): $110,000 - 142,000
Remote/Other Metros (Geo B,C,D): $89,000 - 128,000

Reporting to:
Office Director

Overview Of Role

The Project Manager will maintain a primary focus on practice related services (management of the delivery of all project management related services) and a secondary focus on internal business operations (active engagement with business development, financial management, and staff development matters). Has significant independent responsibility for assignments including entire projects, or a portion of a project as determined by the project lead of office manager. The Project Manager should have the ability to identify opportunities within a project that will add value and help successfully accomplish the client’s desired project outcome.

Essential Functions

Responsible for the management of the Client and project team. Delivers projects that meets the Clients project goals and outcomes.
Serve as liaison with clients, assist clients with all project-related decisions
Plan, organize, and direct the project management functions through all phases of a project – Preconstruction – Closeout:
Preconstruction – Building the A&E team, design management, schedule management, constructability review, budget development and cost control, contract administration, construction bidding and planning, and permitting strategy and process.
Construction - management of the contractor from buyout, procurement, risk management, quality assurance, safety, and overall project execution. Maintain budget and schedule control.
Closeout – manage the closeout process of the project that meets the project specifications

Maintains and produces cost and status reports that meets the Clients objectives
May manage and mentor an internal team of project support (Project Engineers and Administrators) or work independently.
Contributes to team performance by collaboration and effective communication.
Contributes to and understands the clients desired project outcomes, identifies opportunities to add value to accomplish the desired outcomes.
Adds to team effort by accomplishing other duties as assigned

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a positive proactive approach to the role and will be committed to delivering customer service excellence.

Bachelor’s Degree in Construction Management, Architecture or Engineering, related field, or relevant experience.
5+ years’ experience in a variety of building types and construction management through all phases of construction.
Excellent communicator both verbally and write, practical and logical qualities; good problem-solving skills, strong numeracy, and financial management skills; ability to write clear and precise reports and relate complex information to a diverse range of people; able to inspire and manage diverse teams. Proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite of programs including Microsoft Project.

Physical Requirements And Working Conditions

Often work in an Indoor office environment. Equipment used includes computers and standard office machines. Essential physical tasks include: the ability to work on a computer and the ability to answer and speak on a telephone.

Sitting
Standing for long periods of time
Walking, carrying, pushing, stooping, crouching, and pulling

WE HAVE CREATED A WORLD WHERE ART AND SCIENCE ARE BEST FRIENDS

Known is a modern marketing company engineered for the unprecedented opportunities and challenges facing marketers today. We are about 200+ people strong, pairing PhD data scientists with award-winning creatives, strategists, engineers, and expert research teams to produce some of the most innovative and cutting-edge creative work in culture. We believe that when creative truly collaborates with science, strategy, and technology, amazing things can happen.

That belief has earned Known top industry recognition, including being named 2025 ADWEEK Midsize Agency of the Year. Furthermore, Ad Age touted that “Known may be the ultimate example of a full-service agency,” and honored us with top ten status on The Agency A-List for 2024 & 2025 , and as Ad Age’s Data & Insights Agency of the year for a record third year in a row. Without our incredible partnerships with our clients, spanning across the leading brands in finance, technology, entertainment, media, CPG, real estate, and many other categories, honors like this could not be possible, and also have helped us earn additional awards and recognitions over the years like: Emmys, Clios, Effies, Cannes Lions Awards, ProMax Agency of the Year, Fast Company’s World Changing Ideas, Digiday’s 2025 Best AI Platform and Digiday’s Most Innovative Media Agency , to name a few.

We couldn’t create this award-winning work without seeking out and hiring the best talent. What does it mean to be a Knowner? We are curious innovators, knowledge-hunters who are constantly challenging ourselves to do better and be better for our clients, for our team and for our world at large. Our offices around the U.S. are open and while most of our people work in a hybrid setting, we are a distributed workforce with a number of Knowners working remotely.

But Enough About Us, Let's Talk About You

Known is looking for a Project Manager to join the Studios practice. The Project Manager will be responsible for seeing projects through from concept to final delivery across Experiential, AV, Digital, Social and Print/OOH. They will engage key stakeholders appropriately through the process, build and manage timelines and budgets, interface directly and regularly with clients, and ensure the on time, on strategy and on budget delivery of all projects. A full job description is included below:

Own a single workstream within Experiential — design, video content, premiums, locations, etc. — from creative development through final production and delivery
Manage teams through all phases: concepting, creative development, design, QC, and final delivery
Act as the primary point of contact with Account Management and clients on project status and timing
Schedule and conduct internal/external kick-offs and internal SLT/client reviews, ensuring work stays on track and on-brand, and distribute notes to the team
Log client feedback and brand guideline updates, and ensure they carry through to the work
Partner with creative, account, and strategy teams to develop briefs, timelines, decks, and other resources per workstream
Build and maintain master project calendars and workbacks for your workstream, collaborating with stakeholders to track and recalibrate schedules against client briefs, feedback, and deliverable trackers
With input from the creative team and Head of Project Management, draft SOWs outlining initiatives, milestones, and deliverables
Maintain a Master Event Playbook, updated in real time with all event elements, technical specs, and brand standards
Own the Run of Show, serving as primary point of contact for timing and transitions
Identify, order, and manage inventory of event supplies and specialized materials
Manage third-party vendors and support broader vendor communications, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery
Track workstream budget and COGS, reporting updates to the Sr PM
Support the Head of Project Management with internal billing and invoicing
Maintain a proactive and positive attitude

What You Have Done/Who You Are

You have experience delivering high-quality campaigns for industry-leading companies, including Experiential, AV, Digital, Social, Print, OOH and Live Action
You have hands-on experiential production background: creative development, workbacks, vendor management, and on-site execution
You possess an exceptional ability to manage long-term, multi-million dollar engagements and multiple project tracks with a firm command of project management processes and methodologies
Likewise, you are experienced in managing quick, nimble, short-term engagements with smaller, more multi-disciplinary teams
You have a deep understanding of 360 campaign and production lifecycles
You are comfortable owning budget and COGS tracking for a workstream and flagging risk early
You are a collaborative, organized, and motivational project manager
You have a demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
You are proactive, resourceful, and professional with good soft skills
You have exceptional organizational skills
You have worked in a client-facing capacity previously and feel comfortable doing so

YOUR BACKGROUND INCLUDES

5-7+ years of project management or production experience in a fast-paced and integrated agency environment

SOME OF OUR PERKS

Unlimited paid time off
401k with company matching and no vesting period
Generous medical plan
Paid parental leave
Company-wide events and retreats

ONE LAST THING TO ASK YOURSELF

All this might sound great, but you’re probably still wondering, “Would I be a good fit for Known?” or “Would Known be a good fit for me?” Our culture is propped up by four values that we aspire to every day: We are one team. We see the good. We never stop learning. There’s always a better way. At Known we are setting out to build something more than just a company. We are building a legacy filled with exceptionally talented people with a kaleidoscope of backgrounds, experiences, and origin stories who feel encouraged and empowered to bring their whole selves to work, and to partner with us in molding and shaping our culture through our values.

jobs.description:
As a member of the Information Services Department, the IS Project Manager will manage and execute technology projects to improve business results and client experience. The IS Project Manager is responsible for coordinating across the overall program, scope, risk and schedule management and troubleshooting.

Essential Functions

Work with business teams to complete project intake, define project scope and objectives, timelines, budgets, and deliverables.
Manage projects, develop project plans, allocate resources, and monitor performance deliverables to ensure timely completion of projects.
Participate in requirements gathering meetings in a way to ensure the end solution meets the requestors “needs” versus “wants”.
Effectively communicate your project plans to cross-functional team members and management.
Coordinate resources and timetables with business departments and IS teams.
Gather critical information from meetings with various stakeholders to make necessary project adjustments and produce useful visuals and reports when necessary.
Partner with business teams to create User Acceptance Test plans and serve as a liaison between technical and business teams when conducting the testing.
Identify and resolve issues in project plans and schedules.
Communicate project status consistently (weekly/bi-weekly as appropriate) with project team and stakeholders enabling informed decision-making.
Report and escalate issues to management as needed.
Create and maintain comprehensive project documentation.
Manage multiple projects at once.

Additional Functions

Special Projects, as assigned.

Education

Experience

5 years of IT industry experience
5 years of project management experience

Excellent analytical, logical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent project management and organization skills.
Strong leadership and people skills to establish and maintain effective working relationships with peers, managers and clients.
Strong professional communication both written and verbal.
Highly organized with attention to detail and excellent follow-through skills.
Experience with both agile and waterfall project management methodologies.
Gather requirements and process mapping experience required.
Strong ability to multi-task.
Proactive, self-motivated with a high level of ownership and drive to achieve goals.
Skill to document complex systems and procedures.

Global perspective with experience executing major live events both domestically and internationally.
Expert communication skills with the ability to navigate matrixed corporate structures and deliver crisp updates to premium stakeholders.

Project management skills, rather than technical skills, are key to this role, though a strong technical background is often required to manage competing interests. The position may require occasional work at the client site.

Scope and Organizational Responsibility

Oversees the operation of a single department or "unique entity" within the organization. A "unique entity" is defined as any function that requires management (with or without direct reports) and exists only once within the organization. In some instances, this manager may be responsible for a functional area without any subordinate employees.

Plans, organizes, and controls resources within the department or unique entity, and participates in the creation of operating plans that support the organization's overall strategic plan. Manages, potentially through subordinate supervisors, the coordination of activities across a section or department, with responsibility for results including costs, methods, and staffing.

Key Responsibilities

Manage the full project lifecycle, overseeing schedules and budgets to ensure goal attainment.
Receive assignments in the form of objectives and determine how to allocate resources to meet schedules and goals.
Provide guidance to team members within the latitude of established company policies.
Recommend changes to policies and establish procedures that affect the immediate organization.
Lead cooperative efforts among members of a cross-functional project team.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Involves extensive interaction with sales, systems engineering, product development, and other members of cross-functional teams. Frequently interacts with subordinate supervisors, customers, and functional peer group managers, typically on matters spanning functional areas, other company divisions or units, or the relationship between customers and the company.

Decision-Making and Impact

Erroneous decisions or failure to achieve results will add to costs and may impact the short-term goals of the organization.

Who We Are

With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility.

What We Need

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to join our Program Management team within our PMO organization. Your job will be to lead complex, cross-functional automation programs that bring new warehouse automation solutions from concept through customer deployment. You'll work across engineering, product, operations, sales, and customer teams to drive execution, align stakeholders, and ensure successful delivery of innovative automation solutions.

What We Do

The Program Management team is responsible for bringing Symbotic's automation technology to customers through successful planning, execution, and delivery. The team partners across engineering, operations, and customer-facing organizations to coordinate complex technical programs, manage risk, and ensure our solutions deliver measurable business value.

What You'll Do

Lead complex, cross-functional technical programs that deliver automation solutions into customer distribution and warehouse environments.
Drive program execution from concept through deployment by coordinating engineering, product management, operations, supply chain, finance, and customer implementation teams.
Partner with technical and business stakeholders to define program scope, priorities, schedules, risks, and success metrics.
Translate customer and market requirements into scalable program plans that leverage Symbotic's existing platform while supporting new capabilities and technologies.
Serve as a key customer-facing technical partner, building strong relationships while aligning internal teams to deliver on customer commitments.
Establish program governance, monitor execution, proactively identify risks, and drive issue resolution to ensure successful program delivery.

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related engineering discipline required. Master's degree or other advanced engineering degree strongly preferred.
Minimum of 8 years of technical experience leading large, complex engineering or automation programs.
Experience delivering automation, robotics, warehouse, manufacturing, industrial equipment, or other complex hardware/software systems.
Proven ability to lead large cross-functional programs involving engineering, operations, product management, supply chain, and customer-facing teams.
Strong customer-facing experience with the ability to communicate effectively across technical teams, executive leadership, and external stakeholders.
Excellent program planning, risk management, and organizational skills, with a track record of driving programs to successful completion.

Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com.

jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Remote Work Location:
This position may be performed remotely from Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Missouri, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee
. Candidates must reside in one of these states to be considered.

General Description Of Position

Clearwave is scaling its fiber build program from ~500,000 to 1,000,000 homes passed over the next 4–5 years. The Project Manager, Market Expansion
role stands up the Market Expansion function's PMO/Expansion Operations capability; the connective tissue that gives leadership visibility into the market pipeline, keeps cross-functional teams, and turns a fast-scaling, multi-team effort into something trackable, reportable, and governable. This is a build-from-near-zero role: there is no existing PMO function today, limited legacy reporting to inherit, and no established tool stack. The first 3–6 months are about building the operating system for the whole team.

Duties And Responsibilities

Market Funnel Management & Stage-Gate Tracking: own the operating cadence for tracking markets through every stage of the funnel (Full Opportunity Universe through Build-Active and post-build) and hold functional partners accountable to stage-gate criteria.
Pipeline Reporting & KPI Management: build, run, and manage the reporting that feeds recurring governance meetings (ex. Expansion Leadership Meetings and Market Approval Committee). To include pipeline coverage ratios (qualified and engineered buffer) and at-risk market flags.
RACI Governance & Meeting Facilitation: own the RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed) document end to end. Build it, keep it current as the org. evolves, surface ownership gaps or overlaps, and facilitate the cross-functional meetings where it gets used and revised.
Engineered Pipeline Coverage Monitoring: track the qualified pipeline coverage ratio and the engineered buffer separately, and flag early when falls below tolerance.
Executive Reporting: prepare and present pipeline health, build portfolio and progress, and KPI materials for the VP, CRO, and executive audiences as needed.
Cross-Functional Coordination: serve as the connecting point across Market Intelligence & Selection, Market Development, and Government Relations; the person who knows how every piece of the funnel fits together operationally.

Bachelor's degree in business, analytics, project management, or a related field preferred.
5+ years (Project Manager) or 8+ years (Senior Project Manager) of experience in a PMO, program/portfolio management, or business operations role, ideally supporting a capital-intensive build, construction, infrastructure, or network deployment function.
Demonstrated experience building reporting or pipeline-tracking systems from scratch; not just operating an existing one.
Advanced proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, and at least one pipeline/PM tool (Smartsheet, Airtable, Salesforce or similar).

Description -

Program Manager - Products & Services Privacy

Job Summary

This role is responsible for leading and managing privacy projects and enable the HP Products & Services organizations in meeting global privacy, data protection, AI governance, and regulatory compliance obligations. The Program Manager serves as the operational backbone of the privacy organization, driving program execution, portfolio management, stakeholder engagement, project governance, reporting, and continuous process improvement.

The role partners closely with Privacy Advisors, Legal, Engineering, Product Management, Security, Compliance, Data Governance, and business stakeholders to ensure privacy initiatives are prioritized, tracked, communicated, and delivered effectively. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in program management, cross-functional coordination, executive reporting, operational excellence, and organizational change management.

Success in this role requires balancing multiple initiatives, driving accountability across stakeholders, identifying and mitigating risks, and ensuring leadership has visibility into program health, compliance readiness, and strategic priorities.

Responsibilities

Program & Portfolio Management

Lead the planning, execution, and governance of privacy and compliance programs across HP Products & Services initiatives.
Manage a portfolio of privacy initiatives, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, resource availability, and regulatory commitments.
Develop and maintain program roadmaps, project plans, milestones, dependencies, and delivery schedules.
Establish and drive project governance structures, operating rhythms, and reporting mechanisms.
Ensure initiatives progress according to established timelines and proactively address obstacles, risks, and resource constraints.
Coordinate activities across multiple workstreams, teams, and business units to ensure successful execution.
Monitor project health and drive corrective actions when milestones or objectives are at risk.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communications

Build strong relationships with business leaders and operational teams to facilitate collaboration and program success.
Drive stakeholder alignment on priorities, timelines, deliverables, and decision-making processes.
Prepare executive-level presentations, status reports, dashboards, and briefing materials for leadership reviews.
Facilitate governance meetings, steering committees, project reviews, and stakeholder discussions.
Communicate program progress, key risks, dependencies, and escalations to leadership and cross-functional teams.
Manage stakeholder expectations and drive accountability for commitments and action items.

Operational Excellence & Process Improvement

Identify opportunities to streamline privacy operations through standardization, automation, and process improvements.
Create and maintain program documentation, procedures, playbooks, templates, and operating guides.
Establish consistent methodologies for project intake, prioritization, status reporting, and resource management.

Risk Management & Compliance Coordination

Identify, assess, monitor, and communicate program risks, issues, dependencies, and mitigation plans.

Coordinate cross-functional activities related to privacy assessments, regulatory implementations, audits, certifications, and governance reviews.
Ensure privacy programs maintain appropriate documentation and evidence to support internal and external reviews.

Escalate significant risks and blockers to leadership with recommended mitigation strategies.

Analyze trends and provide leadership with actionable insights regarding risks, priorities, workload, and business impact.

jobs.description:
Location
: Hybrid, New York

Medidata follows a hybrid office policy in which employees who are hired for an in-person position are expected to work on site a certain number of days per week following Company policy.

About our Company
:

Medidata is powering smarter treatments and healthier people through digital solutions to support clinical trials. Celebrating over 25 years of ground-breaking technological innovation across more than 38,000 trials and 12 million patients, Medidata offers industry-leading expertise, analytics-powered insights, and one of the largest clinical trial data sets in the industry. More than 1 million registered users across approximately 2,300 customers trust Medidata's seamless, end-to-end platform to improve patient experiences, accelerate clinical breakthroughs, and bring therapies to market faster. A Dassault Systèmes brand (Euronext Paris: FR0014003TT8, DSY.PA), Medidata is headquartered in New York City and has been recognized as a Leader by Everest Group and IDC. Discover more at www.medidata.com. Listen to our latest podcast, from Dreamers to Disruptors, and follow us at @Medidata.

About the Team
:

We are seeking a dynamic Project Manager to lead successful project initiatives that create lasting improvements in patient and site experiences and internal engagement efforts.

Reporting to the VP, Research Site Engagement, this role is ideal for an individual with a strong foundation in project management and relationship building. The Project Manager is responsible for the overall relationship management of projects and day-to-day activities. The function also ensures that Medidata is able to deliver patient, site, and employee insights projects and services on time and within budget through effective management of Medidata resources. This role requires a strategic thinker capable of operationalizing our "Insights - as- a - Product" model.

Responsibilities:

Utilize and Oversee Project Management software solutions (WRIKE) to organize and execute plans and projects that drive internal and external engagement around patient, sites, and employee insights.
Operational Architecture: Drive the creation, development, and standardization of Wrike blueprints and automated dashboards to provide real-time visibility into program delivery, KPIs and program health.
Strategic & Custom Project Management: Lead the end-to-end lifecycle for complex, cross-functional strategic projects. This includes developing custom project plans for both internal mission-alignment efforts and client-facing engagements.
Data-Driven Operational Excellence: Implement rigorous project documentation standards that support the commercialization of OSIE insights, ensuring deliverables are "audit-ready" and consistent with our global OSIE model
Lead project delivery to ensure that all deliverables are tracked and that documentation is current
Manage project expectations and communications, and ensure overall satisfaction
Strategic Reporting: Act as the operational pulse for OSIE leadership, ensuring that project tracking, forecasting, and budgeting directly support our goals, ensuring onetime delivery and superior customer satisfaction.
Manage project financials including forecasting, project budget, and accuracy of invoicing
Create and maintain accurate and current project documentation
Raise and track work requests with other departments as needed
Document minutes/action items during all project team meetings; conduct appropriate follow-up as necessary
Manage issues and risks driving appropriate resolution and mitigation
Provide proactive communication to all stakeholders
Assure compliance with Medidata's standard project management methodologies, quality management system
Support development of sales orders and change orders
Deliver workshops and lead client meetings
Insights Delivery: Partner with leadership to transform raw patient, site, and employee feedback into high-value, AI-assisted data assets. Ensure every project initiative contributes to our centralized intelligence database.

Your Competencies:

Requires only general instruction for routine assignments, and some coaching/mentoring on more complex assignments
Preference for a basic understanding of clinical research (pharma/device/biotech) and of clinical research SaaS technology
Demonstrate good verbal/written communication and organizational skills
Exhibit time management skills along with strong collaboration and teamwork
Experience in leading project teams and meeting project timelines
Self-motivated and able to assume responsibility in a professional manner
Experience with creating and delivering presentations
Operational Mindset: Demonstrated ability to build and maintain sophisticated project management infrastructure (e.g., Wrike, Asana, or similar) to scale operations and ensure global replicability.
Analytical Aptitude: Ability to translate qualitative human experiences (patient/site/employee feedback) into quantitative metrics and actionable data assets.
Strategic Agility: Experience managing both internal engagement programs and external client-facing projects with a focus on commercial value and ROI

Qualifications:

4-year college degree or equivalent (analytic discipline a plus) preferred
Minimum of 2 years experience in clinical/biomedical and/ or software development environment preferred
3-5 years of experience in project management, operations, or business intelligence, preferably within a high-growth environment, clinical research organization (CRO), or software/tech sector.
Project Management Foundation: Demonstrated experience building or optimizing operational workflows. Proven ability to move functions to scale by developing SOPs, RACI matrices, and standard intake frameworks
Analytical Rigor: A background in an analytical discipline is required. Must demonstrate experience in transforming raw, qualitative feedback (e.g., patient, site, or employee data) into high-value, commercialized data assets or strategic reports
Familiarity with AI-driven synthesis tools (e.g., NotebookLM) and project management platforms (e.g., Wrike)

As with all roles, Medidata sets ranges based on a number of factors including function, level, candidate expertise and experience, and geographic location. Pay ranges for candidates in locations other than New York City, may differ based on the local market data in that region.

The salary range for positions that will be physically based in New York is $96,000- $128,000.

Base pay is one part of the Total Rewards that Medidata provides to compensate and recognize employees for their work. Most sales positions are eligible for a commission on the terms of applicable plan documents, and many of Medidata's non-sales positions are eligible for annual bonuses. Medidata believes that benefits should connect you to the support you need when it matters most and provides benefits, including medical, dental, life and disability insurance, 401(k) matching, family leave, flexible paid time off; and 10 paid holidays per year.

Note:
Please be on the lookout for job scams. Medidata recruiters will never ask applicants for monetary compensation, credit card, or banking details.

Equal Employment Opportunity
:

In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at Medidata are based on merit, qualifications and abilities. Medidata is committed to a policy of non-discrimination and equal opportunity for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical or common conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, familial status, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, military service, application for military service, genetic information, receipt of free medical care, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Medidata will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

YOUR TASKS

FORVIA - HELLA is seeking its next great Project Manager to join our growing team. The primary function of this role is to take ownership full functional program management of next generation body systems.

About Us

FORVIA - HELLA is is a listed, internationally positioned automotive supplier operating under the umbrella brand FORVIA. Within this factual group, HELLA stands for high-performance lighting technology and automotive electronics. At the same time, the Company covers a broad service and product portfolio for the spare parts and workshop business as well as for manufacturers of special-purpose vehicles with its Lifecycle Solutions business group. jobs.title: Program Manager, Data Governance and Stewardship, US Based
jobs.description:
Come Join ReSource Pro!

Your Role...

ReSource Pro is seeking a Data Governance and Stewardship Lead establishes and maintains the frameworks, standards, and practices that support the integrity, security, compliance, and appropriate use of ReSource Pro’s data. The role translates data governance principles into practical policies, controls, stewardship practices, and data quality standards that can be consistently applied across a complex, data-intensive environment.

The role works cross-functionally with Data Strategy, Technology, Security, Legal, Compliance, and business stakeholders to define and maintain governance standards for how data is collected, classified, accessed, used, retained, and retired. The Data Governance and Stewardship Lead also supports data quality, lineage, documentation, and stewardship practices that enable the effective use of data for analytics, reporting, automation, and AI.

The role applies strategic and hands-on expertise to establish and maintain data governance practices, translate complex governance requirements into practical policies and guidance, and support consistent adoption and accountability across the organization.

All remote positions are based in the United States, and candidates must reside within the U.S. to be eligible for consideration.

In this role, you will...

Build and Maintain the Data Governance and Stewardship Framework

Develop, document, and maintain data governance policies, standards, procedures, and controls that support the appropriate collection, classification, storage, access, use, retention, and retirement of data.

Define and maintain data ownership, accountability, stewardship, and quality responsibilities across business and functional areas.

Establish practical and scalable governance practices that can be consistently applied across a complex, data-intensive organization.

Maintain clear documentation of governance requirements, decision rights, standards, and operating practices.

Partner with data owners, stewards, and cross-functional stakeholders to implement governance standards and resolve data-related issues.

Develop guidance and education that help stakeholders understand and fulfill their data governance and stewardship responsibilities.

Drive Data Quality, Lineage, and Data Lifecycle Management

Define and maintain data quality standards, rules, and processes for critical data assets.

Establish monitoring and control mechanisms to identify data errors, gaps, inconsistencies, and other quality issues.

Partner with data owners and stewards to investigate root causes, prioritize remediation, and improve data quality over time.

Maintain data lineage and documentation to improve traceability from source systems through downstream use.

Support the development and maintenance of data catalogs, business glossaries, metadata, and other documentation that improve understanding and accessibility of governed data.

Help ensure data assets can be traced, understood, and appropriately governed throughout their lifecycle.

Monitor adherence to established data governance and quality standards and communicate findings, risks, and remediation needs to relevant stakeholders.

Support Data Privacy, Security, Client Commitments, and Responsible Data Use

Partner with Security, Legal, Compliance, and other stakeholders to support data privacy, security, risk management, and regulatory requirements.

Translate contractual and client-specific data requirements into clear governance standards, controls, and operating practices.

Support governance of how client and company data may be accessed, used, stored, shared, retained, and retired.

Maintain appropriate documentation and evidence to demonstrate adherence to applicable data requirements and commitments.

Identify and escalate governance risks, gaps, and potential areas of non-compliance.

Partner with analytics, technology, and AI teams to ensure data used for automation, analytics, and AI applications meets applicable governance, privacy, security, quality, and documentation requirements.

Support governance practices that promote responsible and explainable use of data in AI-enabled solutions.

Monitor Adoption and Continuously Improve Governance Practices

Develop metrics, reporting, and other mechanisms to monitor governance adoption, data quality, and areas of risk or improvement.

Track adherence to data governance standards and support remediation where practices fall short.

Serve as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert on data governance and stewardship questions.

Promote data literacy and effective stewardship practices through clear documentation, training, and engagement.

Facilitate collaboration among data owners, stewards, and technical teams to resolve governance and data quality issues.

Continuously refine governance practices as regulations, client requirements, business needs, and technology evolve.

Teamwork & Collaboration (Standard)

Foster a respectful and collaborative environment by upholding professionalism and engaging in constructive and respectful conversations.

Support a positive workplace culture by promoting open, solution-oriented communication, encouraging teamwork, and maintaining a focus on shared goals and productivity.

What You Need to be Successful...

Educational Background:
Bachelor’s degree in Data Management, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

Working Experience Required And Preferred

5–8 years of experience in data governance, data stewardship, data management, data quality, or a related discipline.

Experience Working In The Insurance Industry Preferred.

Experience supporting data governance for analytics, automation, machine learning, or AI use cases.

Familiarity with data governance frameworks, data management best practices, or relevant industry standards.

Experience implementing or improving data governance programs in a growing or changing organization.

Behavioral/technical skills; Competencies

Hands-on experience developing, implementing, or maintaining data governance frameworks, policies, standards, and controls.

Experience establishing practices related to data quality, classification, access, retention, privacy, or lifecycle management.

Working knowledge of data privacy, security, regulatory, and compliance requirements in a regulated or data-intensive environment.

Experience with data catalogs, metadata management, data lineage, data quality tools, or related data management technologies.

Strong data fluency, including the ability to understand data structures, relationships, sources, and downstream use; experience with SQL is preferred.

Ability to translate complex governance, privacy, security, and data management requirements into clear policies and practical guidance.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes and drive sustainable remediation.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Strong attention to detail and a disciplined approach to documentation, process, and follow-through.

Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and influence stakeholders across functions without direct authority.

Technological proficiency – able to learn, utilize, and navigate a variety of external and internal systems

Travel (% of travel time; domestic or international) :
5% travel: Domestic for company meetings, global every 1-2 years

Your Compensation… 

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of the total compensation package that also includes annual bonus eligibility, benefits, and other opportunities at ReSource Pro. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, geography, and balancing internal equity relative to other ReSource Pro employees. This is a remote position, and the salary range for most locations for this role is $11.25-$23.94 per hour. The salary range may vary based on experience and on the specific geographic location in which the candidate resides.

Your Benefits & Perks…

100% paid employee health insurance available on Day 1 
Eligible for all medical, dental, and vision benefits on Day 1 
Remote positions are Internet stipend-eligible 
401k with employer match, vested on Day 1 
HSA/FSA available 
Long Term and short-term disability employer-provided 
Generous PTO plan with paid holidays + floating holidays 
Development and growth opportunities 
Comprehensive wellness program and prioritization of employee health 

Your Interview Process…

To be considered for this position, please submit your application. If you meet the qualifications for the role, a member of our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch to schedule an interview via zoom.

The Standard Interview Process Includes

Behavioral interview with Talent Acquisition
Online talent assessment
Hiring Manager interview
Additional interview steps may be added depending on the position or if further evaluation is needed.

Disclosure: Candidates are evaluated at each step of the process. As a result, not every candidate will complete all steps in the process.

About ReSource Pro

Focused exclusively on the insurance industry, ReSource Pro is a trusted strategic operations partner to insurance organizations seeking to increase their productivity and profitability. With a global team of more than 10,000 employees, ReSource Pro operates at the critical intersection of people, process, technology, and data to serve more than 1,800 clients across the carrier, broker, and MGA segments – consistently earning a +96% client retention rate for over a decade. It offers expert advisory services, proven business process management optimization and transformative data and technology solutions. For the 15th time since 2009, it was recognized in 2024 by Inc. 5000 as one of the fastest growing companies in the US.

Data Hall Design includes the physical infrastructure design workstreams required to prepare data halls for scalable OCI deployment, including structured cabling, fiber infrastructure, low-voltage systems, physical networking dependencies, construction handoffs, colocation readiness, and operational handoff milestones.

Align stakeholders around goals, owners, timelines, risks, trade-offs, and decision points.

Upper-Intermediate or Advanced English (both written and spoken) for leading client workshops.

Drive Strategic AI Initiatives: Actively advocate for and embed AI capabilities into project strategies to maximize outcomes, maximize ROI, and unlock new business value for clients.

Crisis24 is a global, AI-enhanced provider of travel risk management, mass communications, critical event management, crisis-security consulting, personal protection solutions and global medical concierge capabilities, allowing prominent organizations, disruptive brands and influential people to operate with confidence in an uncertain world. At Crisis24, we don't just offer jobs – we offer missions. We recruit the very best from the military, intelligence agencies, academia, law enforcement, medicine, or any of our areas of specialty. We protect more than places. We protect people, reputations, and lifestyles, with integrity, discipline, discretion, and purpose. Whether you're stepping into civilian life after service, seeking personal or professional growth, or bringing specialized expertise to a higher calling, we match your ambition with real opportunity. Do the most important work of your career, helping safeguard the world's most important organizations and individuals against risk.

More information is available at https://www.crisis24.com/careers

Intelligence Analyst (Analyst III)

Location:
Onsite – Phoenix, Arizona

Division:
Embedded Intelligence Services (EIS)

Schedule:
Full-time: 7-3 Business Hours, Monday-Friday

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Intelligence Analyst with deep expertise in global intelligence, threat assessment, and enterprise risk management to support a major embedded client engagement. The ideal candidate will bring at least five (5) years of intelligence experience, advanced analytical tradecraft, and demonstrated success operating in complex, client-facing environments. This individual will serve as a senior member of the embedded team, providing strategic insight, mentoring junior analysts, and delivering high-impact intelligence products aligned to executive and operational decision-making. Occasional travel and after-hours support may be required.

Position Overview

Reporting to the EIS Intelligence Manager and working closely with client leadership, the Intelligence Analyst will support the Security Operations Center (SOC) activities for a client. The analyst will integrate geopolitical, protective, and security intelligence into decision workflows by providing forward-looking, actionable insights that mitigate risk to personnel, assets, operations, supply chain continuity, and reputation. This role requires strong independent judgment, the ability to manage complex intelligence requirements, and the capability to guide analytical standards across the team while maintaining a collaborative, non-managerial posture within the client environment.

What You Will Work On

Strategic Intelligence Analysis

Conduct anticipatory geopolitical, security, and protective intelligence analysis aligned to client priorities. Deliver tailored intelligence products, including horizon scanning reports, scenario forecasts, executive SITREPs, and impact assessments. Integrate global monitoring into risk decision workflows, identifying both threats and emerging opportunities.

Protective & Security Intelligence

Lead open-source, deep web, and social media monitoring to identify and assess threats to executives and enterprise leadership. Conduct Persons of Interest (POI) investigations, threat actor assessments, executive vulnerability reviews, and due diligence reports. Produce travel threat assessments, route assessments, event security assessments, and site-specific risk evaluations.

Operational Support & Incident Response

Monitor global events in real time and assess operational impact. Support crisis response and emergency incident management in accordance with established best practices and client SOPs. Triage client intelligence requests and deliver timely, decision-ready analysis.

Collaboration & Advisory Support

Serve as a strategic intelligence partner within the SOC environment, aligning intelligence priorities with organizational objectives. Liaise with client stakeholders to understand operational footprint, evolving risks, and intelligence requirements. Mentor analysts in research methodology, structured analytic techniques, writing standards, and briefing delivery. Contribute to continuous improvement of workflows, intelligence products, and playbooks. Support tracking of production metrics and program performance.

Additional Support

Provide ad hoc briefings, executive support, and special analytical projects as required.

What You Will Bring

Education

Bachelor’s degree required.

Experience

5+ years of experience in intelligence analysis, geopolitical risk, protective intelligence, incident response, or enterprise security. Experience supporting senior stakeholders in a corporate, government, or consulting environment. Demonstrated experience mentoring analysts and leading complex analytical projects.

Skills & Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of the intelligence cycle and structured analytic techniques. Strong expertise in OSINT collection, global risk monitoring, and investigative methodologies. Exceptional analytic writing and executive briefing skills. Experience producing strategic intelligence products for senior decision-makers. Familiarity with intelligence and risk management platforms (e.g., Crisis24, Everbridge, Dataminr, Ontic, etc.). High proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and mapping/visualization tools (Google Earth, GIS platforms). Strong client engagement skills and ability to manage expectations in high-stakes environments. Ability to operate independently, prioritize competing demands, and maintain quality under pressure. Foreign language proficiency and international experience are advantageous.

Additional Requirements

Must work onsite in Phoenix, Arizona. Flexibility to support 24/7 mission requirements, including occasional evening or weekend coverage. Occasional travel may be required. Successful completion of background check and writing/technical aptitude assessments required.

Important Note About This Position

This position focuses on geopolitical risk, global threat intelligence, and monitoring events that could disrupt client operations, including political, economic, social, and security factors, as well as natural events such as severe weather and other disasters. The role emphasizes qualitative research, investigative analysis, and intelligence reporting rather than technical, IT, cybersecurity, data analytics, or business intelligence functions. Potential applicants with primary experience in technical or data-centric fields should carefully consider whether this role aligns with their background.

Information Security

Protect the data and systems of Crisis24 and its stakeholders by adhering to policies, reporting incidents and potential problems, completing regular training, and identifying opportunities for improvement.

Crisis24 is dedicated to equal opportunity in employment. We are committed to a work environment that celebrates diversity. We do not discriminate against any individual based on race, color, sex, national origin, age, religion, marital or parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any factors protected by applicable laws.

Ideally you will have the judgement to take the best from agile and waterfall playbooks and know when to use what to deliver outcomes on time and to budget.

You will also people manage another Project Manager and a Business Analyst who may be working on your project or on other change priorities.

Location: This role is in Queenstown only. Being present and connected to stakeholders is key to success here, so there is an expectation of being on-site or in-office a minimum of three days per week.

About The Opportunity

A chance to join a purpose-led South Island organisation where sustainability and conservation matter

A broad portfolio of technology-enabled change across systems, cyber, AI enablement, upgrades and reviews
End-to-end ownership from early discovery through to delivery, adoption and benefits realisation

Description -

Program Manager - Products & Services Privacy

Job Summary

This role is responsible for leading and managing privacy projects and enable the HP Products & Services organizations in meeting global privacy, data protection, AI governance, and regulatory compliance obligations. The Program Manager serves as the operational backbone of the privacy organization, driving program execution, portfolio management, stakeholder engagement, project governance, reporting, and continuous process improvement.

The role partners closely with Privacy Advisors, Legal, Engineering, Product Management, Security, Compliance, Data Governance, and business stakeholders to ensure privacy initiatives are prioritized, tracked, communicated, and delivered effectively. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in program management, cross-functional coordination, executive reporting, operational excellence, and organizational change management.

Success in this role requires balancing multiple initiatives, driving accountability across stakeholders, identifying and mitigating risks, and ensuring leadership has visibility into program health, compliance readiness, and strategic priorities.

Program & Portfolio Management
